messages:

Subject: Defining success for our MAP: ClearMed POC

Soojin / team —

Thanks again for the demo last week. ClearMed leadership wants a short, testable mutual action plan we can use to judge the POC and decide on a commit. Can you send a draft that lists:
- Concrete success criteria (what "good" looks like) with numeric thresholds where possible
- Exit gates / pass-fail rules for the POC
- Specific acceptance tests we can run (and who provides evidence)
- A recommended close timeline (milestones & signoffs)

We've attached our current scope doc (POC-Scope-v3.pdf) — the team will want throughput and latency SLAs, and a short list of quality checks for the classification tasks. Budget and procurement are on a separate track but we need the MAP to be precise before we schedule executive signoff.

Can you get a draft back by EOD Friday PT?

Tom
VP Product, ClearMed

[attachment: POC-Scope-v3.pdf (pdf)]

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@clearmed.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Defining success for our MAP: ClearMed POC

Tom —

Appreciate the clarity. Attached is a first-pass MAP draft focused on measurable proofpoints and a compact acceptance test inventory (see smoke-test-cases.xlsx). Key sections below; full doc attached.

Summary (high level)
- Goal: Validate Redwood Inference for ClearMed triage & summarization pipeline over a 4-week POC.
- Close decision: Go / No-go based on the acceptance checklist and evidence pack.

Success criteria (quantified where possible)
1) Latency: p95 generation latency <= 300ms for first-stream token at 512 context under 1-to-1 load profile (measured from API gateway).
2) Throughput: sustained 60 requests/minute with tail-latency SLO (p99) < 800ms during steady-state.
3) Quality: 90%+ top-1 label agreement vs ClearMed labeled gold set (sample of 1k cases).
4) Safety/Precision: false-positive rate for sensitive-class labels <= 2% on the audit sample.
5) Reliability: platform uptime >= 99.5% during POC window (ex excludes scheduled maintenance).

Exit gates / pass-fail rules
- Gate A (SMOKE): System is reachable, auth works, simple generation flows return valid JSON schema (accept on 3 consecutive runs) — prerequisite to start deeper tests.
- Gate B (PERF): If Latency or Throughput thresholds miss by >20% after one optimization cycle => escalation and remediation; POC enters "remediation" state (30% extension possible) or No-go.
- Gate C (QUALITY): If label agreement < 85% on the gold set after two rounds of prompt & model tuning => No-go.

Acceptance tests (examples)
- Smoke: Basic auth + sample inference (owner: ClearMed devs, evidence: API logs + sample outputs).
- Regression: Run 1k-case gold set; compare top-1 labels (owner: ClearMed QA; evidence: scored CSV).
- Latency profile: Synthetic load with representative requests (owner: Redwood infra; evidence: p95/p99 logs + Grafana link).
- Concordance: Clinical-sample concordance checks for edge cases (owner: joint; evidence: annotated comparisons).
- Security checklist: KMS key in place, network isolation verified, SOC2 summary provided (owner: Redwood security).

Artifacts we will deliver
- smoke-test-cases.xlsx (test descriptions + expected outputs)
- SOC2-summary.pdf (security artifacts summary)
- Evidence folder (logs, scored CSVs) in Drive

Proposed timeline & signoffs
- Week 0 (Kickoff): Environment provisioned, smoke tests (3 days)
- Week 1: Perf baseline & 1st tuning cycle
- Week 2: Full regression run (1k gold sample) & safety checks
- Week 3: Remediation window (if needed) & executive review prep
- Decision: Week 4 executive signoff (Go/No-go) — signers: ClearMed Eng. Director, ClearMed VP Product, Redwood Sales Lead

Next steps: Ben & I will add a short acceptance-runbook (owners & tooling). Can we confirm the 1k gold set availability and whether ClearMed wants a separate privacy/PII masking evaluation?

Thanks — draft attached.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

[attachments: smoke-test-cases.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@clearmed.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Defining success for our MAP: ClearMed POC

Nice draft — a few concrete additions from infra & success ops: 

1) Add sample-size & statistical confidence notes for quality gate: 1k sample gives ~2-3% margin; recommend stratified sampling (80/20 stable/edge).
2) Instrumentation: we will provide a per-request trace id in headers for every test run; ask ClearMed to capture trace id in their runner so we can correlate logs.
3) Canary & rollback triggers: if p95 > 1.2x target for >15 minutes under production-like traffic, auto-fallback to smaller model variant; documented as explicit rollback action.
4) Evidence checklist (minimal): Golden CSV, perf traces, Grafana perf dashboard snapshot, error-rate histogram, and for any No-go a 1-page RCA.

Small wording tweak to Gate B: call out a single "optimization cycle" definition (2 business days of tuning + one config change). If still failing, trigger remediation.

I'll drop the runbook into the Drive folder and link to the Grafana snapshot template. Confirming owners: Redwood infra (Ben) for perf tests; Redwood security (Marissa) for SOC2 evidence.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
